# @zakkster/lite-form

Headless reactive forms for `@zakkster/lite-signal`. Form STATE as fine-grained
signals; bind to any DOM/renderer. No virtual DOM, no template compiler. Typing
in one field of a 100-field form runs exactly one validator. A form-level
schema (Zod/Yup-shaped) is hoisted into a single computed that runs once per
keystroke, not once per field.

ESM-only. Node >= 18. Single file `Form.js`, 1565 lines, ~21 KB minified.
Peer dependencies: `@zakkster/lite-signal ^1.5.0` and
`@zakkster/lite-project ^1.4.1` (the projection engine the value core rides in
BOTH modes -- the import is static, so it must be installed even if you never
pass `source`).

## Install

    npm i @zakkster/lite-form @zakkster/lite-signal @zakkster/lite-project

## Imports

    import { createForm } from "@zakkster/lite-form";

## Exports

`createForm` and `VERSION` (the package version string).

### `createForm(config?) -> Form`

Build a reactive form. Eagerly allocates one signal + per-field computeds for
every leaf in `initialValues`, every key in `validators`, and every key in
`fieldOpts`. Returns a `Form` handle.

Config (all optional):

- `initialValues: object` -- default `{}`. Dotted paths supported; leaf values
  become the initial signal values.
- `validators: Record<string, (value, ctx) => string | null>` -- per-field. The
  `ctx.get(path)` accessor reads another field's value AND records a dependency.
- `validate: (values) => Record<string, string | null>` -- form-level schema.
  Hoisted to ONE computed; runs once per keystroke.
- `fieldOpts: Record<string, { parse?, format? }>` -- per-field input transforms,
  applied at the `props()` boundary.
- `validateOn: "change" | "blur" | "submit"` -- error display gating (does NOT
  affect `isValid()`, which is always live). Default `"change"`.
- `onSubmit: (values) => void | Promise<void>` -- invoked from `submit()` if
  valid. Called untracked (its signal reads don't leak into the caller).
- `registry: createRegistry() handle` -- scope every signal/computed to this
  registry instead of the default. Bind with that registry's `effect`.
- `source: live keyed source` -- ENGINE mode. Project a live keyed source (e.g.
  a lite-store proxy) instead of the detached baseline. Edits stage as overlays
  (source untouched); `commit()` writes through. `dirty` = overlay presence: an
  authoritative source write under an un-overlaid field never flips dirty; a
  conflicting write under an overlaid field stays masked. Requires the
  `@zakkster/lite-project ^1.4.1` peer.
- `validatorsAsync: Record<string, (value, ctx) => Promise<string | null>>` --
  per-field ASYNC lane beside the sync validator. Last write wins: a per-field
  sequence drops stale settlements (resolve or reject) whole -- no signal
  write, no error flash. The latest rejection surfaces as the field error
  (never silently valid). NO timers inside lite-form.
- `asyncSources: Record<string, (field, ctx) => (() => any)>` -- reader FACTORY
  for the async lane's trigger (called once at construction, form-owned).
  Default: the field's own value. The lite-debounce recipe:
  `username: (fld) => debounce(() => fld.value(), 300)`.
- `arrays: Record<string, ArrayConfig>` -- keyed field arrays (1.4.0), keyed by
  the dotted path of an Array in `initialValues` (must resolve to an Array,
  else TypeError). `ArrayConfig = { key: (item, i) => string, validators?,
  validatorsAsync?, asyncSources?, fieldOpts? }` -- sub-config keyed by
  SUB-PATH within a row (no wildcard grammar). `key` derives each row's stable
  identity (once per row per seed/add/re-seed, never per keystroke; non-empty,
  no ".", hostile segments rejected, duplicates throw). Row validator ctx
  gains `local(sub)` (reads this row's sibling field, tracked). Default mode
  only: `source` + `arrays` throws at construction. An UNDECLARED array stays
  a plain leaf value exactly as before.

## Field interface (`form.field(path)`)

Fields are reactive state for one form field. Created eagerly for declared
paths; created lazily on first `.field(path)` for undeclared paths.

    field.path                  // string
    field.value                 // WritableSignal<T>  (value() reads+tracks; value.peek() untracked)
    field.error                 // ReadSignal<string|null>  reveal-gated display
    field.rawError              // ReadSignal<string|null>  always-live validity
    field.dirty                 // ReadSignal<boolean>  !Object.is(value(), initialRef); in-place mutation does not flip it, set(newRef) does
    field.touched               // ReadSignal<boolean>  blurred at least once
    field.isValidating          // ReadSignal<boolean>  latest async check unsettled; async-validated fields only (shared frozen false otherwise)
    field.set(v)                // write
    field.blur()                // mark touched (does not validate; affects display reveal)
    field.reset()               // back to initial value; clears touched
    field.props()               // { value, onInput(ev), onBlur() } -- spread onto an <input>

`props().onInput` knows about checkbox inputs (`ev.target.type === "checkbox"`
-> uses `.checked` instead of `.value`).

## Form interface

    form.field(path)            // get / lazy-create a Field; on a DECLARED array path the next segment must be a live row key (same Field as row(key).field(sub)); index or non-live-key segments throw
    form.array(path)            // ArrayHandle for a declared array (1.4.0): keys() tracked frozen snapshot / length() / structureDirty() tracked; row(key) -> { key, field(sub) } identity-stable; add(item, atIndex?) -> key; remove(key); move(key, toIndex); undeclared path or unknown key -> TypeError
    form.values()               // untracked snapshot; own-walk materialization, each leaf deep-copied; uncopyable runtime value -> TypeError naming the path
    form.setValues({path: v})   // batched multi-set; NOT atomic under a throwing entry (a hostile or illegal path throws loud, but writes applied before it land) -- 1.3.0 semantics, now documented
    form.reset()                // restore initialValues; clear touched, submitAttempted, submitError
    form.commit(path?)          // fold dirty values into baseline (all, or one path); unregistered path -> TypeError; committed fields pristine, reset() now targets committed state; values deep-copied through the whitelist
    form.toPatch()              // [{path, from, to}] of exactly the dirty paths (from=baseline, to=current); field set back to initial ref excluded; plus ONE {path, structure:{order, added:[{key,index,value}], removed}} entry per structurally-dirty declared array -- added rows carry their full value there and never emit field entries (no overlap); untracked + read-only, safe in an effect
    form.reinitialize(next, policy?) // 1-arg: re-seed like initialValues (deep-copied + whitelist-validated BEFORE any state change -- atomic TypeError on bad input); drops every edit, absent paths re-seed undefined, clears touched + submit state; declared arrays re-seed FULLY (keys re-derived from next, all row state cleared, order adopted). 2-arg MERGE (default mode only; source mode throws -- use reconcile; a form with DECLARED ARRAYS throws -- keyed row merge is a recorded future design): pristine ADOPTS n; dirty + (Object.is(n,d) || policy(n,d) === true) ECHOES (overlay cleared, pristine at n); else CONFLICT (draft kept masking n, baseline re-seeds underneath: reset() lands n, toPatch().from === n); touched clears on ADOPT/ECHO, survives CONFLICT; submit state never written; throwing policy is atomic
    form.reconcile(policy?)     // source-mode merge: drop exactly the overlays the live source agrees with (default Object.is); legal in default mode (no-op under the default policy by design); the policy runs LATCHED (1.4.0) -- any mutating form call from inside it throws TypeError, the same purity window as the 2-arg merge
    form.submit(ev?, opts?)     // Promise<boolean>  preventDefault + validate + onSubmit; opts.patch: true posts toPatch() instead of values() (empty patch still submits [])
    form.isValidating           // ReadSignal<boolean>  true while ANY field's async check is unsettled
    form.isValid                // ReadSignal<boolean>  always live
    form.isDirty                // ReadSignal<boolean>  any field differs from initial
    form.isSubmitting           // ReadSignal<boolean>  async onSubmit in flight
    form.submitError            // ReadSignal<Error|null>  last operational throw
    form.submitAttempted        // WritableSignal<boolean>  set true to force-reveal all errors
    form.dispose()              // free every signal/computed; idempotent

## Field arrays (1.4.0)

Declare a path in `arrays` and its rows get stable keys: values, dirty,
touched, error, and async state travel with the ROW across moves, never with
the index. Laws:

- One addressing model per declared path: index paths (`rows.0.name`),
  `field("rows")`, and whole-array writes throw TypeError directing to the
  row API. `setValues({"rows.<key>.name": v})` on a live key is legal.
- Reorder is order-only: `move()` re-runs no validators and writes no row
  field (torture-proven with instrumented counters); `keys()` returns a new
  frozen snapshot exactly once per structural mutation.
- Added rows: presence is structure-dirty; their fields compare dirty against
  the ADD SEED; `commit()` promotes (row enters baseline, order folds);
  `reset()` drops added rows and restores removed baseline rows + order.
- Removal is teardown: the row's signals + async lanes are disposed (an
  in-flight settlement becomes a no-op; a PENDING lane releases its
  isValidating slot), fields leave the map, projection slots are pruned.
  Distinct-key add/remove churn holds activeNodes flat under the gate.
- Single-leaf rows (a primitive/array/Date item): exactly ONE field, addressed
  as `<arrayPath>.<key>` with no sub segment. A named sub under a single-leaf
  row, or an empty sub on an object row, throws TypeError (it would be
  invisible to values()/toPatch() while still counting toward validity).
- Schema mode: the scratch tree materializes declared arrays in order;
  index-based schema error keys translate index -> key per run (a moved row's
  error follows the CURRENT order -- the schema sees current values).

## Validation modes

`validateOn` controls when `field.error()` becomes non-null. `isValid()` is
unaffected and always reflects true validity:

- `"change"` (default) -- reveals once `dirty()` is true
- `"blur"` -- reveals once `touched()` is true
- `"submit"` -- reveals only after `submitAttempted()` flips true

`submit()` sets `submitAttempted = true`, which force-reveals everything
regardless of mode. `reset()` clears it again.

## Submit lifecycle

`submit(ev?)` does, in order:

1. `ev.preventDefault()` if `ev` is provided
2. `submitAttempted.set(true)` -- reveals all errors
3. If `!isValid()` (read untracked) -> return `false`. No call to `onSubmit`.
4. If no `onSubmit` configured -> return `true`
5. `isSubmitting.set(true)`, `submitError.set(null)`
6. `await onSubmit(values())` -- called inside `untrack`
7. On resolve -> return `true`
8. On `ReferenceError` / `SyntaxError` -> `console.error` + re-throw (structural
   bugs, not legitimate submission outcomes)
9. On other throws (including `TypeError` from fetch network failure) ->
   `submitError.set(err)`, return `false`
10. Finally -> `isSubmitting.set(false)`

## Key invariants

- **Eager field allocation.** All declared fields exist after `createForm()`
  returns. Lazy creation is supported via `field(undeclared)` but is slower
  on first access.
- **Schema is hoisted.** With `validate` configured, the schema runs exactly
  ONCE per keystroke via a shared computed. Each field reads `schema[path]` as
  an O(1) lookup with Object.is cutoff.
- **Reveal-gated display, live validity.** `field.error()` returns null when
  not revealed; `field.rawError()` always reflects real validity. `form.isValid()`
  reads `rawError`s, not `error`s.
- **Pristine fields don't run validators.** When `field.error()` short-circuits
  on the reveal gate, it never reads `rawError()`, so the validator is never
  called for that field. Only dirty/touched/submit-attempted fields validate.
- **`submit` and `onSubmit` are untracked.** Calling `submit()` from inside an
  effect doesn't subscribe that effect to internal form state. Your `onSubmit`
  can read other signals (auth.token, etc.) without leaking dependencies.
- **`registry` option is fully respected.** All signals, computeds, and
  internal batching/untrack go through the provided registry. Default registry
  stays untouched.
- **`dispose()` is idempotent and complete.** All owned signals/computeds are
  freed; field map cleared. Calling twice is a no-op.
- **Hostile path segments are rejected (v1.0.1).** `__proto__`, `constructor`,
  and `prototype` are forbidden as path segments everywhere a path enters the
  form (`createForm` config keys, `field()`, `setValues()`, validator
  `ctx.get`). They throw a `TypeError`; nothing is written, nothing is cached.
- **The baseline is unreachable (v1.1.0).** `initialValues` is deep-copied
  once at `createForm` and never read again; object leaves are copied again
  at field seed, `reset()`, and snapshot materialization. No caller-reachable
  reference is ever the reset target: in-place edits through `field.value()`
  cannot corrupt the caller's object or the baseline.
- **Construction-time config validation (v1.1.0).** The copy walk whitelists
  leaf material (primitives, arrays, Date, plain-object branches); functions,
  Map/Set, RegExp, typed arrays, class instances, and symbols throw TypeError
  at `createForm` naming the path. Cycles throw TypeError (previously a stack
  overflow on branch cycles). Any OWN key named `__proto__` / `constructor` /
  `prototype` anywhere in `initialValues` throws -- including
  `{"__proto__": {}}` from JSON.parse, which forms no leaf path and slipped
  the 1.0.1 segment guard.
- **Snapshot boundary throws typed (v1.1.0).** `values()` and schema-mode
  reads materialize through lite-form's own walk; an uncopyable RUNTIME field
  value (a function set after construction, say) throws a TypeError naming
  the field path -- replacing the old late DataCloneError. `set()` itself
  stays unchecked: any value is fine reactively; the snapshot is the door.
- **Lazy fields are effect-safe (v1.1.0).** `field(undeclared)` under a live
  tracking context allocates inside the form registry's `createRoot()`, so a
  re-running effect cannot dispose the field's signals. Requires the
  lite-signal >= 1.5.0 owner API (hence the peer floor).
- **`submit()` is NOT internally deduped.** Two concurrent `submit()` calls
  fire `onSubmit` twice, both racing on the same `values()` snapshot. Guard
  via `isSubmitting` (UI), `@zakkster/lite-throttle` (hotkeys/programmatic),
  or an early-return on `isSubmitting.peek()`. See the recipe below.
- **Engine projection, baseline still unreachable (v1.2.0).** The value core
  rides a `@zakkster/lite-project` projection (`fromAccessors` over per-field
  seed copies + a `baselineRev` signal; per-key overlay signal + projected
  computed). The public API is frozen and every S1 contract holds verbatim:
  `source.get` returns the field's seed copy, never a baseline reference; commit
  deep-copies in; the baseline is never caller-reachable.
- **Overlaid === dirty via clear-on-initial (v1.2.0).** `field.set(v)` with
  `Object.is(v, seed)` clears the overlay instead of staging it, so "overlaid"
  coincides with "dirty"; `form.isDirty` rides the engine's tracked
  `dirtyCount()`.
- **Scratch-tree validate() ownership (v1.2.0).** Schema mode no longer clones
  per keystroke; the object handed to schema `validate()` is a form-owned,
  transient scratch tree (leaves written in place, object leaves by reference,
  rebuilt only on `reinitialize`/`commit`). Retaining or mutating it is
  undefined behaviour. Public `values()` still returns a fresh deep copy.
- **Source-mode dirty = overlay presence (v1.2.0).** In `createForm({ source })`
  engine mode, edits stage as overlays (source untouched); an authoritative
  source write under an un-overlaid field is not an edit and never flips dirty;
  a conflicting write under an overlaid field stays masked. `commit()` writes
  through.
- **Peer floor `@zakkster/lite-project ^1.4.1` (v1.2.0).** 1.4.0 was falsified
  by lite-form's t6 (a ~40 B/op hot-path context allocation in the engine's
  `get`/`peek`/`set`, invisible to its own pool-census gate) and fixed upstream
  as 1.4.1 with the transient witness ported. See `decisions/0002-engine.md`.
- **The merge table (v1.3.0).** `reinitialize(next, policy)` is atomic (a
  validation OR policy throw mutates nothing -- verdicts are pre-scanned before
  any state change) and runs in one batch with exactly one baselineRev bump.
  Object.is(n, d) force-echoes BEFORE the policy runs (an equal pair must never
  stay overlaid -- protects overlay === dirty); only `=== true` confirms.
  Deep-copied payloads mean object leaves never auto-confirm under the default
  policy -- pass a structural policy for object-valued fields. The policy must
  be PURE: any mutating form call from inside the merge window throws a
  TypeError (re-entrancy latch -- verdicts are pre-scanned against a snapshot;
  applying them over mutated state would be silent corruption).
- **The async ordering law (v1.3.0).** Per-field monotone sequence; a stale
  settlement is dropped whole; `isValidating` is true exactly while the latest
  is unsettled; `isValid` is STRICT-FALSE while any verdict is pending (so
  `submit()` refuses during validation with the existing gate); `dispose()`
  mid-flight settlements are no-ops. No timers anywhere in Form.js -- debounce
  is the caller's via the `asyncSources` lite-debounce recipe.
- **Off-cost async seam (v1.3.0).** A form with no `validatorsAsync` allocates
  no lane machinery and keeps the 1.2.0 keystroke numbers byte-for-byte
  (hoisted sync/async body variants chosen at construction); sync-only fields
  on a mixed form share one frozen `false` for `isValidating`. Async-validated
  keystroke: 629.703 B/op recorded (promise machinery; settlements outside the
  window).
- **LF-12 fixed (v1.3.0, latent since 1.2.0).** `field.dirty()` read before a
  `commit()` (or forced-echo merge row) stayed true after it: the fold is
  value-preserving, so the Object.is cutoff never re-ran the cached computed
  while `initialRef` was re-captured underneath. `dirty` now tracks
  `baselineRev` (the re-capture notifier) directly.
- **Row identity is the key, never the index (v1.4.0).** A declared array's
  overlay paths are `<arrayPath>.<rowKey>.<sub>`; per-row state (value, dirty,
  touched, error, isValidating) is keyed, `move()` writes order only, and the
  patch surface never emits overlapping entries (added rows ride
  `structure.added` whole). One addressing model per declared path -- index
  and whole-array access throw. Undeclared arrays are byte-identical to 1.3.0.
- **Off-cost arrays seam (v1.4.0).** Array-aware variants of
  values/toPatch/commit/reset/reinitialize/submit/dispose and the validity
  composites are selected at construction (`hasArrays`, the async-seam
  precedent); a form with no `arrays` takes the 1.3.0 paths byte-for-byte
  (t6 floors unchanged). Row-field keystroke: 0.119 B/op GATED at the same
  suite constant as flat/dotted. Structure ops recorded: add+remove pair
  8,855 B/op, move 294 B/op.
- **LF-13 fixed pre-release (v1.4.0, never shipped).** Teardown without a
  notifier: removing the row holding `isValid`'s only live dependency
  orphaned the memoized verdict (the LF-12 class on the validity lane), and
  a lane torn down while PENDING stranded the form-level isValidating
  counter. `rowFieldsValid` now tracks each array's structure revision and
  `teardownRow` releases the pending slot. The transferable rule: a
  short-circuiting computed over a DYNAMIC field population must track the
  population's revision, not only the members it read.

## Recipes

### Sign-in form (vanilla DOM)

    import { createForm } from "@zakkster/lite-form";
    import { effect } from "@zakkster/lite-signal";

    const form = createForm({
        initialValues: { email: "", password: "" },
        validators: {
            email:    (v) => /@/.test(v) ? null : "invalid email",
            password: (v) => v.length >= 8 ? null : "min 8 chars",
        },
        onSubmit: async (vals) => fetch("/api/login", {
            method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(vals),
        }),
    });

    for (const name of ["email", "password"]) {
        const f = form.field(name);
        const inp = document.getElementById(name);
        const err = document.getElementById(name + "-error");
        inp.addEventListener("input", (ev) => f.set(ev.target.value));
        inp.addEventListener("blur", () => f.blur());
        effect(() => { inp.value = f.value(); });
        effect(() => { err.textContent = f.error() || ""; });
    }

### Number input with parse/format

    createForm({
        initialValues: { age: 0 },
        fieldOpts: {
            age: {
                parse:  (raw) => Number(raw),
                format: (val) => String(val),
            },
        },
    });

`props().onInput` calls `parse`; `props().value` returns the `format`'d view.

### Password + confirm (cross-field)

    createForm({
        initialValues: { pw: "", confirm: "" },
        validators: {
            confirm: (v, { get }) => v === get("pw") ? null : "must match",
        },
    });

Typing in `pw` re-validates `confirm`. `ctx.get` records the dependency on
read; no manual subscription required.

### Zod integration

    import { z } from "zod";
    const schema = z.object({
        email: z.string().email(),
        age:   z.number().min(18),
    });

    const form = createForm({
        initialValues: { email: "", age: 0 },
        validate: (values) => {
            const r = schema.safeParse(values);
            if (r.success) return {};
            return Object.fromEntries(
                r.error.issues.map(i => [i.path.join("."), i.message])
            );
        },
    });

The schema runs once per keystroke regardless of field count.

### Yup integration

    import * as yup from "yup";
    const schema = yup.object({ email: yup.string().email().required() });

    createForm({
        initialValues: { email: "" },
        validate: (values) => {
            try { schema.validateSync(values, { abortEarly: false }); return {}; }
            catch (e) {
                return Object.fromEntries(e.inner.map(i => [i.path, i.message]));
            }
        },
    });

### Registry-scoped form (multi-form isolation)

    import { createRegistry } from "@zakkster/lite-signal";

    const reg = createRegistry({ maxNodes: 1024, maxLinks: 4096 });
    const form = createForm({ initialValues, validators, registry: reg });
    // Bind with reg.effect(), not the default effect:
    reg.effect(() => /* read form.field(...).value() */);
    // ...later:
    form.dispose();   // returns reg.stats().activeNodes to baseline

### Force-reveal errors before submit

    form.submitAttempted.set(true);
    // Every field.error() now reads its rawError(); display is no longer gated.

### Dispose on cleanup

    // In a component / effect / route teardown:
    onCleanup(() => form.dispose());

### Surfacing server errors WITHOUT a setFieldError API

    // lite-form has no setFieldError() method -- it doesn't need one. Per-field
    // validators run inside a computed, so any signal they read is TRACKED.
    // Hold the server error in a signal; flip it from your fetch handler.
    const serverErr = signal(null);            // null | "username taken" | ...

    const form = createForm({
        initialValues: { username: "" },
        validators: {
            username: (v) => {
                if (!v) return "required";
                return serverErr() || null;     // tracked -> re-validates on flip
            },
        },
    });

    // After a 409 response:
    serverErr.set("already taken");             // field.error() updates automatically
    // Clear it when the user edits:
    effect(() => { form.field("username").value(); serverErr.set(null); });

    // This pattern is strictly nicer than setFieldError(): no method call, no
    // race between programmatic write and reactive validate, and disposal is
    // automatic (the server signal is just a normal lite-signal handle).

### Defending against double-submit (concurrent submit IS a real footgun)

    // submit() is NOT internally deduped. Calling it twice while one is in
    // flight fires onSubmit TWICE -- both promises return true; both fetches
    // race. Three documented defenses:
    //
    // 1) Disable the submit button via the reactive `isSubmitting` signal:
    effect(() => { btn.disabled = form.isSubmitting(); });
    //
    // 2) Throttle the handler -- @zakkster/lite-throttle is the matching tool:
    const guardedSubmit = throttle(() => form.submit(), { leading: true, trailing: false });
    formEl.addEventListener("submit", (e) => { e.preventDefault(); guardedSubmit(); });
    //
    // 3) Guard inside your own handler with `form.isSubmitting.peek()`:
    function onSubmit(e) {
        e.preventDefault();
        if (form.isSubmitting.peek()) return;
        form.submit();
    }
    //
    // Pick (1) for UI forms (button stays disabled until the request settles),
    // (2) for programmatic / hotkey submits (Enter key in two places).

## Performance (Node 26 measured)

- Create + dispose, small (3 fields): ~205K ops/sec, ~1.8 KB transient, ~0 B retained
- Create + dispose, large (100 fields): ~3.8K ops/sec, ~9.6 KB transient, ~21 B retained
- Keystroke on 1 of 100 fields (per-field validators): **~6.1M ops/sec**
- Keystroke on 1 of 100 fields (form-level schema, hoisted): ~83K ops/sec
- Cross-field validation (pw + confirm): ~21M ops/sec
- Pure-JS handwritten baseline (runs all 100 validators): ~400K ops/sec
- Speedup over handwritten pattern: ~15×

Pool clean: `stats().activeNodes === 0` after every bench run.

## Testing

144 deterministic tests (`node:test`): `npm test`. Plus the torture gate:
`npm run torture` (node --expose-gc --preserve-symlinks test/torture.mjs) which
proves zero-GC keystrokes (@zakkster/lite-gc-profiler) and zero-leak teardown
(@zakkster/lite-leak). `npm run verify` runs both.
